audience.programmeDescription: Dutch Language and Culture at Radboud studies Dutch and Flemish literature, the structure and history of Dutch, and the use of language in communication. It combines textual analysis, literary and linguistic research methods, and independent research.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR can offer sustained literary interpretation and language analysis within a broader humanities and cognitive curriculum. UCR does not reproduce advanced Dutch-language scholarship, Dutch/Flemish literary history or historical Dutch linguistics. The unresolved replacement for the repeated 5-EC module is excluded.

trace: Introduction to Literary Studies directly teaches practical literary interpretation across fiction, poetry, drama and narrative forms. It implements the explicit academic basis “Literary analysis, theory, genres and creative expression”.

The Art of Rhetorical Communication directly develops rhetorical analysis, persuasive writing and speaking. It implements the explicit academic basis “Rhetoric, stylistics, persuasion and communication in public and media settings” and “How do style, rhetoric and media persuade and shape public communication?”.

Modern History provides specific modern historical context for interpreting cultural texts and public discourse. It implements the explicit academic basis “Historical and cultural context, power, identity, heritage and media” and “How do literary and media forms represent identity, history and power?”.

Introduction to Brain & Behavior introduces brain anatomy and psychological theories that support later study of language processing. It implements the explicit academic basis “Language acquisition, processing, cognition, variation and human linguistic capacity” and “How do people acquire, process and use language?”.

Style & Meaning analyses how linguistic choices create meaning, obligation, uncertainty and ideology in literary and non-fiction texts. It implements the explicit academic basis “Literary analysis, theory, genres and creative expression” and “Rhetoric, stylistics, persuasion and communication in public and media settings” and “How do style, rhetoric and media persuade and shape public communication?”.

Rhetoric in Action applies rhetorical theory and public speaking with primary-school pupils, not Dutch subject teaching. It implements the explicit academic basis “Rhetoric, stylistics, persuasion and communication in public and media settings” and “How do style, rhetoric and media persuade and shape public communication?”.

World Myth & Literature studies myth, literary transmission and cultural transformation across historical and global traditions. It implements the explicit academic basis “Literary analysis, theory, genres and creative expression” and “Historical and cultural context, power, identity, heritage and media”.

Introduction to Film & Media develops analysis of film and media as cultural production that shapes identity, power and public meaning. It implements the explicit academic basis “Historical and cultural context, power, identity, heritage and media” and “How do literary and media forms represent identity, history and power?” and “How do style, rhetoric and media persuade and shape public communication?”.

Media Archaeology examines print and pre-digital media as material forms that shape cultural memory and communication. It implements the explicit academic basis “Historical and cultural context, power, identity, heritage and media”.

Introduction to Sociology provides social theories and methods for analysing institutions, identity, inequality and interaction. It implements the explicit academic basis “Historical and cultural context, power, identity, heritage and media” and “How do style, rhetoric and media persuade and shape public communication?”.

Great Literary Works surveys literary forms and historical traditions while developing close reading across periods. It implements the explicit academic basis “Literary analysis, theory, genres and creative expression” and “Historical and cultural context, power, identity, heritage and media”.

Life & Travel Writing studies autobiography, travel writing, identity, memory and cultural self-representation. It implements the explicit academic basis “Literary analysis, theory, genres and creative expression” and “How do literary and media forms represent identity, history and power?”.

From T.V. to TikTok examines how television and social media shape attitudes, narratives and public responses. It implements the explicit academic basis “Historical and cultural context, power, identity, heritage and media” and “How do style, rhetoric and media persuade and shape public communication?”.

The Documentary combines documentary analysis with research, argument and production of a short documentary. It implements the explicit academic basis “Historical and cultural context, power, identity, heritage and media” and “Research design, data analysis and evidence synthesis for language, communication and culture”.

Film & Text analyses adaptation, intertextuality and cross-media narrative between literature and film. It implements the explicit academic basis “Literary analysis, theory, genres and creative expression” and “Historical and cultural context, power, identity, heritage and media”.

Persuasive Communication applies ethical persuasion models to public communication about water, food and energy. It implements the explicit academic basis “Rhetoric, stylistics, persuasion and communication in public and media settings” and “How do style, rhetoric and media persuade and shape public communication?”.

History of Empires examines empire and power as specific historical contexts for cultural production and identity. It implements the explicit academic basis “Historical and cultural context, power, identity, heritage and media” and “How do literary and media forms represent identity, history and power?”.

Modern Sociology studies modernity, imperialism and colonial responses through social theory. It implements the explicit academic basis “Historical and cultural context, power, identity, heritage and media” and “How do literary and media forms represent identity, history and power?”.

Perspectives on Literary Meaning applies feminist, Marxist, minority and psychoanalytic perspectives in a literary research project. It implements the explicit academic basis “Literary analysis, theory, genres and creative expression” and “Historical and cultural context, power, identity, heritage and media” and “Research design, data analysis and evidence synthesis for language, communication and culture” and “How do literary and media forms represent identity, history and power?”.

Creative Communication Laboratory studies and practises poetic form, voice, sonic expression and performance. It implements the explicit academic basis “Literary analysis, theory, genres and creative expression” and “Rhetoric, stylistics, persuasion and communication in public and media settings”.

History Research Seminar develops source criticism and a substantial research paper through historical inquiry. It implements the explicit academic basis “Historical and cultural context, power, identity, heritage and media” and “Research design, data analysis and evidence synthesis for language, communication and culture”.

Psycholinguistics directly studies language acquisition, comprehension, production, bilingualism and language impairments through cognitive neuroscience. It implements the explicit academic basis “Language acquisition, processing, cognition, variation and human linguistic capacity” and “Research design, data analysis and evidence synthesis for language, communication and culture” and “How do people acquire, process and use language?”.

Neurobiology provides neurobiological foundations for the study of language and cognition. It implements the explicit academic basis “Language acquisition, processing, cognition, variation and human linguistic capacity” and “How do people acquire, process and use language?”.

Statistics & Experimental Methods develops experimental design and advanced statistical analysis for behavioural evidence. It implements the explicit academic basis “Research design, data analysis and evidence synthesis for language, communication and culture”.

Perception & Action studies neural mechanisms of sensory processing, perception and action. It implements the explicit academic basis “Language acquisition, processing, cognition, variation and human linguistic capacity” and “How do people acquire, process and use language?”.

Philosophy of Mind examines mind, consciousness, identity and their relation to brain and technology. It implements the explicit academic basis “Language acquisition, processing, cognition, variation and human linguistic capacity” and “How do people acquire, process and use language?”.

Higher Order Functions deepens neurophysiology and studies higher cognition including language, memory and social cognition. It implements the explicit academic basis “Language acquisition, processing, cognition, variation and human linguistic capacity” and “How do people acquire, process and use language?”.

Introduction to Data Science develops data cleaning, visualisation and analysis, including text data. It implements the explicit academic basis “Research design, data analysis and evidence synthesis for language, communication and culture”.

Advanced Research Seminar develops systematic-review and meta-analytic methods for research synthesis. It implements the explicit academic basis “Research design, data analysis and evidence synthesis for language, communication and culture”.

Lifespan Developmental Psychology examines cognitive, biological and social development across the lifespan. It implements the explicit academic basis “Language acquisition, processing, cognition, variation and human linguistic capacity” and “How do people acquire, process and use language?”.

alternatives.label: Literature, rhetoric & cultural interpretation
alternatives.concept: Study literary form, theory and adaptation alongside rhetoric, stylistics, persuasion, media and the historical interpretation of culture, identity and power. Psycholinguistics supplies a direct language-processing strand, while qualitative inquiry supports empirical cultural research. The programme does not offer advanced Dutch proficiency, Dutch grammar, historical Dutch linguistics or a Dutch/Flemish literary-history sequence.
alternatives.labelReason: Six literature courses, six communication courses with qualitative cultural research, four media courses, five history/sociology courses and two cognitive-language courses form the curriculum; the label does not imply advanced Dutch or Dutch literary history.
progression: Literary, rhetorical, historical, brain-and-behaviour, media and sociological foundations precede advanced literary interpretation, adaptation, persuasive communication, documentary production, historical research and Psycholinguistics. All formal prerequisites and exact planned offerings pass; seven 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Language, cognition & public communication
alternatives.concept: Investigate language as a cognitive, social and persuasive practice through Psycholinguistics, neurobiology, perception, development, stylistics, rhetoric, media, sociology and quantitative research. The curriculum addresses language and communication generally rather than reproducing Dutch linguistics, sociolinguistics or advanced Dutch-language study.
alternatives.labelReason: Six communication courses, eight cognition/psychology courses, three media courses, two sociology courses, two literature courses, philosophy and data analysis make language use, processing and public communication the visible centre.
progression: Brain-and-behaviour, rhetoric, literary analysis, introductory Dutch, stylistics and neurobiology precede Psycholinguistics, perception, experimental statistics, public rhetoric, advanced cognition, persuasion, development and research synthesis. All formal prerequisites and exact planned offerings pass; seven 300-level courses are included.
alternatives.distinctness: The first programme is organised around literature, cultural interpretation and historical context, with rhetoric and media alongside it. The second makes language processing, cognition and public communication central, replacing eight literature/history/documentary courses with neurobiology, perception, developmental psychology, experimental methods, philosophy of mind and data analysis. Each programme therefore contains 60 EC not found in the other, above the 30-EC floor.

selection.assessment: Two substantively different responses are retained after review: literary/rhetorical/cultural interpretation and language/cognition/public communication. Both remove beginner Dutch, which cannot carry native academic-language scholarship, and add qualitative inquiry. Eight courses differ in each direction (60 EC); the concepts explain those differences. Historical Dutch linguistics and advanced Dutch teaching lack a sufficiently sustained UCR taught response for the next alternative. Stop at two; no third is fabricated.

blocks: Both directly teach literary analysis; UCR’s introduction is not restricted to Dutch-language literature.
Both examine literature through power and ideology; UCR applies several critical perspectives rather than a Dutch-specific literary corpus.
Both directly address rhetoric and persuasive public communication; UCR does not provide Dutch-specific argumentation training.
Both examine how language choices create meaning across communication and texts; UCR’s stylistics course is not a Dutch-language systems course.
Both directly study persuasive communication; UCR applies the models primarily to climate communication.
Both directly study psycholinguistics and language processing through cognitive and experimental approaches.

notes.text: Radboud Dutch Language and Culture integrates advanced Dutch, Dutch and Flemish literary history, Dutch linguistics, rhetoric and a discipline-specific thesis. UCR can study literature, rhetoric, media, cultural interpretation, Psycholinguistics and basic everyday Dutch, or concentrate on language, cognition and public communication. These are related-fields responses: UCR does not offer advanced academic Dutch, Dutch phonology and syntax, historical Dutch linguistics or a Dutch/Flemish literary-history sequence.
